notes:
One file, index/index.bin, documented at the top of lib/index-format.mjs and in docs/DESIGN.md.
Imports text-analyzer because indexing and lookup both tokenize through it, and corpus-reader
because the gate measures the real corpus through readCorpus.

Why binary and not JSON: JSON postings ran several times the corpus size; the binary layout
holds indexBytes/corpusBytes at 0.3148 (laws/index-size.json). Where the bytes went, in order:
postings 22.1 KB, term dictionary 3.0 KB, offset tables 2.5 KB, doc ids 0.9 KB, lengths 0.2 KB.
Narrowing the three offset tables from u32 to the width their largest entry needs took the
index from 31337 to 28910 bytes (~8%) with no behaviour change.

Next lever if size is ever the binding dimension: the term dictionary offsets are the only
remaining fixed-cost table (one entry per term). A block-skip index — a full offset every 16th
term, scanning within the block — would cut that to about a sixteenth for roughly a hundred
lines of extra code and a slightly slower lookup. Not done: 3% of the index is not worth the
reader complexity at this corpus size. Postings themselves are already ~2 bytes per pair;
beating that needs bit-packing (PForDelta), which is a different contract.

writeIndex serialises the whole file in memory BEFORE it removes the old directory, so a
failure cannot leave a half-written index. Both mutants (stale files surviving a rewrite,
title frequencies dropped from postings) are caught by the gate.
